name: Edward Snowden
contribution: Disclosed documents that transformed public understanding of global electronic surveillance and has continued public privacy advocacy.
whyIncluded: His disclosures produced a durable public-record route into surveillance law, intelligence oversight, encryption and source protection.

sources.label: Freedom of the Press Foundation board

caveat: Inclusion recognises documented disclosure and privacy impact; it does not settle every legal, political or national-security argument surrounding the disclosures.

name: Meredith Whittaker
contribution: Signal president and long-time technology critic focused on privacy, surveillance and institutional power.
whyIncluded: She combines operational leadership of private messaging infrastructure with public resistance to surveillance business models.
caveat: Ranking concerns privacy leadership and documented public work, not endorsement of every opinion.

name: Cindy Cohn
contribution: Long-time EFF lawyer and leader whose work includes cryptography, surveillance, privacy and free-expression cases.
whyIncluded: Legal defence determines whether privacy tools and digital speech remain usable in practice.
caveat: Ranking recognises documented civil-liberties work and does not imply agreement with every EFF position.

name: Ron Deibert
contribution: Founded Citizen Lab, which investigates commercial spyware, cyber-espionage, censorship and digital threats to civil society.
whyIncluded: Citizen Lab produces evidence that can expose otherwise invisible surveillance systems and their operators.
caveat: Ranking recognises evidence-led research; it does not imply every investigated claim has the same confidence or legal status.

name: Nighat Dad
contribution: Founded Pakistan's Digital Rights Foundation and advocates for privacy, free expression and safety for women and vulnerable users.
whyIncluded: Her work extends digital-rights defence into environments where online abuse, censorship and surveillance carry severe real-world risks.
caveat: Ranking recognises documented digital-rights work, not endorsement of every policy position.

name: Bruce Schneier
contribution: Cryptographer and security technologist who has spent decades explaining surveillance, security policy and systemic technological risk.
whyIncluded: Independent security analysis helps the public and policymakers distinguish genuine protection from security theatre and hidden trade-offs.
caveat: Ranking reflects public-interest analysis and does not imply agreement with every policy judgment.

name: Phil Zimmermann
contribution: Created Pretty Good Privacy, helping move strong encryption from specialist circles into public use.
whyIncluded: PGP established that individuals could possess communication privacy without depending on state or corporate permission.
caveat: Ranking recognises encryption history and public impact, not endorsement of every product or later implementation.

name: Adam Back
contribution: Invented Hashcash and has continued building privacy-oriented Bitcoin and peer-to-peer financial infrastructure.
whyIncluded: His work represents the cypherpunk strategy of shifting power through deployed technology rather than permission-based reform alone.
caveat: Ranking recognises documented technical contribution and is not investment advice or endorsement of every corporate decision.

name: Micah Lee
contribution: Created OnionShare and has built tools and reporting practices for secure file sharing, source protection and privacy.
whyIncluded: OnionShare gives users a practical way to exchange files and publish services over Tor without relying on a conventional host.
caveat: Ranking concerns secure-tool development and journalism, not endorsement of every publication or opinion.

name: Nathan Freitas
contribution: Founded Guardian Project and developed tools including Orbot, bringing Tor and secure communications to mobile users.
whyIncluded: Mobile access is essential because many users facing censorship or repression rely primarily on phones.
caveat: Ranking recognises privacy-tool development and does not imply every tool eliminates all operational risk.

name: Eva Galperin
contribution: EFF cybersecurity director focused on malware, surveillance, stalkerware and practical protection for vulnerable populations.
whyIncluded: Her work connects technical security research to people exposed to domestic abuse, repression and targeted surveillance.
caveat: Ranking recognises documented cybersecurity advocacy, not endorsement of every EFF position.

name: Runa Sandvik
contribution: Security researcher known for work on Tor, newsroom security and protecting journalists and sources.
whyIncluded: Press freedom depends on operational security as much as legal rights.
caveat: Ranking recognises security and press-protection work; public role details should be checked against current sources.

name: Cory Doctorow
contribution: Author and activist focused on surveillance capitalism, platform lock-in, interoperability and user rights.
whyIncluded: His work turns technical power structures into public concepts and policy arguments that non-specialists can act on.
caveat: Ranking recognises documented digital-rights work, not endorsement of every political or economic claim.
